biography: Loïc Villiger, a name whispered with increasing respect in the racing world, hails from the small town of Annecy in the French Alps. Growing up, Loïc wasn't initially drawn to motorsports; his passion lay in competitive cycling. However, a chance encounter at a local karting track during a family vacation changed everything. He was immediately captivated by the raw speed and mechanical complexity of the machines. After saving up for a kart of his own, Loïc quickly dominated the local karting scene. His breakthrough came in the French national karting championship, where he secured a surprise victory against seasoned veterans. This victory led to a spot in the Alpine academy, where he has honed his skills and steadily risen through the ranks, impressing everyone with his calm demeanor and consistent performances. Now, on the cusp of even greater opportunities, Villiger is poised to make a significant impact on the world stage.
drivingStyle: Villiger's driving style is characterized by remarkable consistency and calculated aggression. He isn't one for flamboyant overtakes or risky maneuvers, instead preferring to patiently build pressure and capitalize on the mistakes of others. His tire management is exceptional, often allowing him to run longer stints and gain an advantage in the closing stages of a race. He possesses an uncanny ability to remain composed under immense pressure, a trait that has earned him the nickname 'Iceberg' within the Alpine team.

careerHighlight: Winning the French National Karting Championship in 2018 after starting from the back of the grid due to a mechanical issue in qualifying. This was a defining moment in his early career.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead in the final lap of the Formula Regional European Championship race at Monza in 2022, losing valuable championship points.
